### Base policies governing the subjects
`delivery_evt_subscription_billing` (activation, month-end fallback, one charge per cycle, past-due date, grace day-0 counting, no-subscription never past due) → subscription_billing_and_past_due_status rules 1–6 + grace table; `delivery_evt_order_fees` in-force clauses → order_fee_rules rules 1–8; `delivery_evt_order_eligibility` → order_placement_rules rules 1–9; `delivery_evt_refunds` in-force clauses (refund once, dispatched cannot be cancelled, missing-order claim/trace, subscription refunds) → order_fee_refunds_and_missing_orders rules 1–4, subscription_fee_refunds; `delivery_evt_handover` → handover_signature_and_lateness. All carried; untriggered branches (same-day waiver by value, distance fee, redelivery fee, lapsed pricing, other plans' figures) present.

## bijection_verdict

**PASS.** No atom unborne, none borne with changed meaning, no claim without source; retired surface complete and correctly marked; both prerequisite sentences verbatim on their blocked side only.

Policy-side notes (do not change this verdict):
1. `parameter_schema.late_credit_max_per_cycle` still reads "Most late refunds per billing cycle", while the only rule that enforced it as a cap (base `delivery_evt_refunds` late clause) is superseded by `delivery_ext_late_delivery_refund`, which uses the figure only as the frequency-share threshold. The KB renders the schema meaning faithfully (delivery_windows_and_late_credit: "Most late refunds per billing cycle or calendar month" row; bullets "allow … up to 4 late refunds per billing cycle", "up to 2 late refunds a calendar month") and marks the cap clause retired (order_fee_refunds_and_missing_orders). On an untriggered branch (a plan already at its per-cycle figure) a reader meets both readings. Nature: stale parameter meaning after an override on the policy side, not a rendering addition. Not triggered in this task (0 late refunds in the current cycle).
2. `parameter_schema.order_cancel_refund_before_dispatch` still reads "…refunded in full"; the KB's quick reference row reads "has its fees refunded" (without "in full"), consistent with the extended rule that re-uses the flag as the gate of the cancellation refund. Same nature as note 1, resolved by the KB in the direction of the in-force extended rule.
